info.title: Dynasty API
info.description: Read-only cached data for one CFB 27 online dynasty. The dynasty comes from the API key, or for a partner key (cfbp_…) from the Dynasty-Id header. Data is as fresh as the last sync (see /league and /sync). Every authenticated response has a weak ETag built from the league's data version; send it back in If-None-Match to get 304 when nothing changed. Limit: 120 requests a minute per key (burst 60). Typed SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Go: https://dynasty.prestonchoate.dev/developers

get.summary: Rosters, read once a period (each in-game week or stage; a team without one is read on the next sync): ratings, archetype, class, redshirt, dev trait, abilities, skill groups and unspent skill points. User teams by default; on paid plans CPU teams are read too and served with `scope=all` or `team`. `player_key` matches /player-stats.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: Season. Default: the newest cached season

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: Team key. A CPU team's roster needs a paid plan (without one, only user teams match)

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Position, e.g. `QB`, `LEDG` (case-insensitive)

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `user` (default): user teams. `all`: every FBS team, on paid plans (403 `plan_required` otherwise)

304.description: Not modified (If-None-Match matched the data version)

403.description: `plan_required`: `scope=all` without a paid plan; or a partner key whose access to that dynasty was not granted or was revoked

get.summary: Playing Style rankings. Each ranks every school by one stat over one set of players (every WR archetype ranks WR receptions; Pass Protector linemen rank team passing yards), so archetypes that share a ranking are grouped. `stat_value` is each school's value of that stat. KR, PR, LS and gadget archetypes have no Playing Style stat and are left out.

SkillGroup.description: One of a player's skill groups. Tiers 1..`level` are filled, the next `buyable` can be bought with skill points, and the last `locked` are above the player's potential `cap`. A level above the cap came from the player's ratings; nothing can be bought then.

cap.description: Potential: the highest tier that can be bought

buyable.description: Tiers still buyable: `cap - level`, at least 0

locked.description: Tiers above the cap: `max - max(cap, level)`

levels_gained.description: Level change by group since the previous snapshot, where it changed. Levels bought with skill points (the game also auto-progresses players)

points_change.description: Skill points since the previous snapshot: down when spent, up when earned
